sources.title: James Huffman, The Meiji Restoration Era, 1868 to 1889, Japan Society
sources.note: Directly read scholarly institutional essay, especially Sources, Transition and Creating a Modern System. Broad political outline used; erroneous late-1868 resignation and later treaty/conscription dates excluded. Modernized does not mean equally beneficial or universally accessible.

sources.title: Japan Society, Timeline of Modern Japan, 1868 to 1945
sources.note: Directly read dated entries 1868 to 1872. Only years used because the timeline mixes old-calendar and Gregorian dates. Bathing prohibition is an ordinance with documented noncompliance, not proof that mixed bathing ended.

sources.title: Japanese and Russian foreign ministries, Joint Compendium: 1875 exchange treaty, Article 2
sources.note: Directly read historical treaty text in joint compendium. Article 2 exchanges Japanese Sakhalin rights for eighteen Russian-held Kuril islands. Used for historical change, not an endorsement of any present territorial claim. Imported geometry independently decoded in identities.json.

sources.title: Sekine Tatsuhito, The Society of the Northern Extremity of the Japanese Main Island in the Edo Period, Seen through Famine Monuments
sources.note: University repository English abstract, printed page 178, read in full indexed original text. Direct PDF access failed. Query: "Sekine" "Tsugaru" "towers". Reports Tenmei 1783 to 1784 famine, flight, and twelve jointly erected monuments among the ninety-eight associated monuments. Large mortality estimates deliberately omitted.

sources.title: National Diet Library Newsletter 214, A Short History of Wagashi, October 2017
sources.note: Directly read PDF, printed page 6, section 7. Curatorial description of 1854 Toyokuni print and Morisada manko late-Edo vendor performances. These are dated examples, not a claim that every household made or bought identical food.

sources.title: University of Tokyo Faculty of Medicine, History
sources.note: Directly read institutional chronological record, 1858 to 1877. Private practitioner funding, fire and continuation, shogunal sponsorship and institutional merger are explicit. No nationwide vaccination coverage asserted.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Infectious Diseases in Books: Cholera and Tuberculosis
sources.note: Directly read Cholera section: 1858 outbreak and Ogata Koan compilation; 1850s vegetable/fish battle print and market response. Count canonical URL reuse with Imperial Japan card, which uses the later 1880 hygiene booklet. Historical popular beliefs are not medical advice.

sources.title: Ministry of Education, Japan’s Modern Educational System: Middle Level Education for Girls
sources.note: Directly read paragraphs on Tokyo Government Girls School and Kyoto school. Tokyo 38 pupils in 1873, closure 1877; Kyoto English/sewing/handicrafts 1872 and abacus/arithmetic/calligraphy added 1875.

sources.title: Brian Platt, Meiji Era School Attendance tables, Children and Youth in History
sources.note: Directly read George Mason University scholarly primary-source module. First table supplies 1873 primary enrollment percentages, sourced to Platt, Burning and Building (2004). Enrollment is not daily attendance; 1883 village table falls outside this map and is not used.

sources.title: Keio University, 150 Years of An Encouragement of Learning
sources.note: Full bilingual indexed original page read; direct page returned error. Query: site:keio.ac.jp "学問のすゝめ" "An Encouragement" 1872 1876. ABOUT section provides exact title, translation, 1872 first installment, seventeen installments by 1876 and Nakatsu school context. Japanese sample is the university’s typographic title transcription, not a new decipherment of a manuscript.

sources.title: National Diet Library, The Japanese Calendar: Calendar History 2
sources.note: Directly read Meiji era change section. Decision in 1872, effective January 1, 1873, corresponding to what would have been old-calendar December 3. Distinguishes calendar labels from elapsed physical time.

sources.title: Japan Post Holdings, History
sources.note: Directly read corporate institutional timeline, 1871 to 1877. Network, nationwide flat rate, postcards, postal money orders, international mail and savings services. No unsupported claim about universal household access or literacy.

sources.title: National Diet Library Image Bank, Ukiyo-e Depictions of Railways
sources.note: Directly read introduction and catalogued railway prints. Railway opened between Shimbashi and Yokohama October 14, 1872; leading artists depicted it before and after opening. Does not claim that every print is a literal eyewitness drawing.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct phased narrative; no association with tokugawa-shogunate or imperial-japan.
batchIdentityNotes.mapWindow: 1783 to 1878; dateBasis remains map_coverage. First phase begins at imported start, not a national founding.

batchIdentityNotes.evidenceLimits: Keio title and Sekine English abstract checked as full indexed originals after direct fetch failure. All other listed sources directly read. No inferred universal literacy, vaccination, school access or compliance with bathing ordinance. No artificial point years for multi-year historical developments.
